title: AgentDesign: design review for AI coding agents (Mac app)
excerpt: AgentDesign is a design review app for AI coding agents. Your agent draws each screen on your Mac, you point at what's wrong, and every version is kept.
content_html:
For people who build apps with Claude, Codex or Cursor

Your AI coding agent designs first. You review, refine, and keep every version before it becomes code.

Compare versions side by side, check the built app against its design, and keep every change as plain files on your Mac.

Free demo · Every feature · No time limitNotarized by Apple · macOS 13+ on Apple silicon

  • You don’t draw.Your agent draws. You point and approve.
  • Free demo.Every feature. No account, no time limit.
  • Every version kept.Compare any two. See which is live.
  • $99 once.Two computers. No subscription.

How it works

Your agent draws. You approve. Then it builds from the design.

Seven steps, from the first screen to every version kept. Everything here fits in the free demo.

  1. Ask your agent for a screen. It draws it before writing any code.

    Six screens arrive in Screens before any code exists.

  2. When it isn't sure, it shows you options instead of guessing.

    Three ways to answer. You pick one, and your reason is kept with it.

  3. Something's off? Point at it.

    Pin the exact spot. Your agent changes the design and replies.

  4. You approve. Only then does it write code.

    Review what changed, then approve. Only you can approve.

  5. The app is built. Check it against what you approved.

    AgentDesign puts a screenshot of the build beside the design and marks the differences.

  6. Next release: see exactly what changes.

    Compare iOS 1.0 with iOS 1.1: what changed, what is new, what stayed.

  7. Every version of every screen is kept.

    Compare any two, see which is live, and open a screen's whole history.

Proof

Built with AgentDesign.

I'm Hitesh. I build apps with coding agents, and I kept losing track of what my agent had drawn, what I'd approved and what actually shipped. AgentDesign is the tool I wanted: my agent draws every screen first, I point at what's wrong, and every version is kept. Every AgentDesign update is now designed in AgentDesign first, and so is my app Updesh. If something's missing, write to me. I read every message.

· Maker of AgentDesign, Sweden

Video

See AgentDesign in 84 seconds.

From an empty project to an approved screen, a comment and the built app.

Read the transcript →

Who it is for

Not an editor. Your agent designs. You review.

For you if

  • You build with Claude Code, Codex or Cursor.
  • Your app has screens: iOS, Android or web.
  • You have no designer, so your agent guesses.

Not for you if

  • You want to draw by hand. Keep Figma or pen.dev.
  • You are on Windows or Linux today.

What you need

  • An Apple silicon Mac with macOS 13 or later. The app is notarized by Apple.
  • A coding agent. Designing needs one.

Why not just

Why not just...?

...a rules file?

A good idea, and it works well alongside AgentDesign. AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md tells your agent what not to touch. It can’t show you a screen before it’s built, and you can’t point at a button in a text file.

...screenshots and git?

Both show you a screen only after it’s built. AgentDesign adds the step before: your agent draws, you point and approve, and then it writes code. Designs are plain files, so you can put them in git too.

...HTML mockups?

HTML in git gives you browser editing and commit history. AgentDesign keeps your comments on the exact element, your approvals, and every version of each screen in one place.

Compare the two workflows

...a design canvas?

In a canvas, you draw. In AgentDesign, your agent draws and you review. You get the same review step in Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor, for iOS, Android, and web screens. When your agent changes a screen, the earlier version stays, and you can check the built app against what you approved.

Pricing

$99 once. Two computers.

One license covers one person on up to two Macs. Another year of updates is optional and costs $19.

Apple silicon · macOS 13 or later. Prices exclude VAT.

What is AgentDesign?

AgentDesign is a design review app for AI coding agents. Your agent (Claude Code, Codex or Cursor) draws each screen of your app in it before writing any code. You point at what’s wrong and approve it, then the agent builds. Every version of every screen is kept on your Mac.

Does it replace Figma?

Keep Figma if your team designs by hand. In AgentDesign you don’t draw anything: your agent draws each screen, and you point at what’s wrong and approve it. AgentDesign vs Figma compares the two.

Where are my designs stored?

AgentDesign saves designs on your Mac. A connected coding agent may send the designs it reads to its AI provider.

Which agents work with it?

Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, and other coding agents that can connect to apps on your Mac through MCP, a common standard for that. You connect yours with one click inside the app, and undo it with one click.

Can I use it without an agent?

Partly. You can look and comment. Designing needs an agent.

What does it cost?

$99 once, one person, two computers, a year of updates. Then $19 a year for new versions, if you want them.

What is in the free demo?

Every feature, 1 project, 2 versions, no time limit. Unlimited: $99, paid once.

Does the app go online?

The app goes online to activate your license and check for updates. You can turn update checks off. AgentDesign saves designs on your Mac. A connected coding agent may send the designs it reads to its AI provider.

Windows or Linux?

Not yet. Windows and Linux are planned.

Try it on your own app today.

The free demo has every feature. You don't need an account.

Your AI coding agent designs first. You review, refine, and keep every version before it becomes code.

  • You don’t draw.Your agent draws. You point and approve.
  • Free demo.Every feature. No account, no time limit.
  • Every version kept.Compare any two. See which is live.
  • $99 once.Two computers. 没有订阅。

它是如何运作的

Your agent draws. 你批准。 Then it builds from the design.

Seven steps, from the first screen to every version kept. Everything here fits in the free demo.

  1. Ask your agent for a screen. It draws it before writing any code.Six screens arrive in Screens before any code exists. The Sprout project starts empty. The Sprout project starts empty.Six screens arrive, drawn before any code.Open Home to see the first draft.
  2. When it isn't sure, it shows you options instead of guessing.Three ways to answer. You pick one, and your reason is kept with it. Your agent opens an option board. Your agent opens an option board.Three ways to answer: word list, picture cards, typing.You pick B, and your reason is kept.
  3. Something's off? Point at it.Pin the exact spot. Your agent changes the design and replies. Pin Continue and say what's wrong. Pin Continue and say what's wrong.Your comment goes to the agent.It moves Continue to the top and replies.Resolve it when it's right.
  4. 你批准。 Only then does it write code.Review what changed, then approve. Only you can approve. Review the change, outlined for you. Review the change, outlined for you.Approved. Now your agent writes the code from the design.
  5. The app is built. Check it against what you approved.AgentDesign puts a screenshot of the build beside the design and marks the differences. Open the built app beside the design. Open the built app beside the design.Check is blue in the build, violet in the design.
  6. Next release: see exactly what changes.Compare iOS 1.0 with iOS 1.1: what changed, what is new, what stayed. iOS 1.1 is planned: 2 changed, 2 new. iOS 1.1 is planned: 2 changed, 2 new.Compare 1.0 and 1.1, changes outlined.
  7. Every version of every screen is kept.Compare any two, see which is live, and open a screen's whole history. Home: first draft, iOS 1.0 live, iOS 1.1 building. Home: first draft, iOS 1.0 live, iOS 1.1 building.iOS 1.0 is marked live. Nothing is thrown away.

Why not just

Why not just...?

...a rules file?

A good idea, and it works well alongside AgentDesign. AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md tells your agent what not to touch. It can’t show you a screen before it’s built, and you can’t point at a button in a text file.

...screenshots and git?

Both show you a screen only after it’s built. AgentDesign adds the step before: your agent draws, you point and approve, and then it writes code. Designs are plain files, so you can put them in git too.

...HTML mockups?

HTML in git gives you browser editing and commit history. AgentDesign keeps your comments on the exact element, your approvals, and every version of each screen in one place.

Compare the two workflows

...a design canvas?

In a canvas, you draw. In AgentDesign, your agent draws and you review. You get the same review step in Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor, for iOS, Android, and web screens. When your agent changes a screen, the earlier version stays, and you can check the built app against what you approved.

What is AgentDesign?

AgentDesign is a design review app for AI coding agents. Your agent (Claude Code, Codex or Cursor) draws each screen of your app in it before writing any code. You point at what’s wrong and approve it, then the agent builds. Every version of every screen is kept on your Mac.

Does it replace Figma?

Keep Figma if your team designs by hand. In AgentDesign you don’t draw anything: your agent draws each screen, and you point at what’s wrong and approve it. AgentDesign vs Figma compares the two.

Where are my designs stored?

AgentDesign saves designs on your Mac. A connected coding agent may send the designs it reads to its AI provider.

Which agents work with it?

Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, and other coding agents that can connect to apps on your Mac through MCP, a common standard for that. You connect yours with one click inside the app, and undo it with one click.

Can I use it without an agent?

部分。 You can look and comment. Designing needs an agent.

What does it cost?

$99 once, one person, two computers, a year of updates. Then $19 a year for new versions, if you want them.

What is in the free demo?

Every feature, 1 project, 2 versions, no time limit. Unlimited: $99, paid once.

Does the app go online?

The app goes online to activate your license and check for updates. You can turn update checks off. AgentDesign saves designs on your Mac. A connected coding agent may send the designs it reads to its AI provider.

Windows or Linux?

还没有。 Windows and Linux are planned.
